320	#### Step 6c — Populate custom fields (api-type ObjectActions)
321	
322	A connector activity has a **parent-field-driven schema** when its valid input fields are not fixed in static metadata but are computed at design time by running an api-type ObjectAction against the IS Element Service. Examples: Jira's `Create Issue` schema depends on the project + issue type; Snowflake's `executeQuery` response columns depend on the SQL string; Dataservice V3's entity field set depends on `tenantEntityName`. The activity persists the parent-field values in `essentialConfiguration.customFieldsRequestDetails` so the runtime can replay the schema-fetch ObjectAction on each invocation. The CLI passes this through verbatim.
323	
324	**How DAP determines support — check both metadata locations.** An api-type action may live at either:
325	
326	- Top-level `objectActions[]` with PascalCase `ActionType: "Api"` (older shape, e.g. Jira `GenerateSchema`)
327	- `connectorMethodInfo.design.actions[]` with lowercase `actionType: "api"` (newer shape, e.g. Dataservice V3 `FetchObjectMetadataTenant`)

329	The dispatcher matches `ObjectActionType.Api === 'api'` (case-sensitive lowercase string) — both shapes go through the same `_processCustomFieldsRequestAction` code path with no per-connector branching. Always inspect both locations from `registry get` output before deciding the connector has none.

334	- **`source: method`** — the action is declared at the operation level and matched against the operation's HTTP method (typically CRUD activities).

359	**Token encoding rule.** Tokens are encoded via `NamingHelper.getValidIdentifier` (the IS-side identifier sanitizer) before being used as `parameterValues` keys, so they match design-property names at lookup time. Substitutions (applied longest-first):
360	
361	| Match in token | Encoded as |
362	|---|---|
363	| `:::` | `_sub_` |
364	| `[*]` | `_array` |
365	| `::` | `_sub_` |
366	| `.` | `_sub_` |
367	
368	Examples: `fields.project.key` → `fields_sub_project_sub_key`; `items[*]` → `items_array`; `tenantEntityName` → `tenantEntityName` (unchanged). When in doubt, inspect a working `.flow` for the encoded form.
369	
370	> **`customFieldsRequestDetails` is COMPLEMENTARY to `bodyParameters` / `queryParameters`, not a substitute.** Same parent-field values must appear in BOTH places, with different keys:
371	>
372	> | Location | Purpose | Key shape |
373	> |---|---|---|
374	> | `bodyParameters` / `queryParameters` / `pathParameters` | Runtime input — what the connector actually sends to its API | **Raw** field names (e.g. `fields.project.key`, `tenantEntityName`) |
375	> | `essentialConfiguration.customFieldsRequestDetails.parameterValues` | Design-time replay cache — drives the parent-field-driven schema fetch when the activity is re-opened or re-validated | **Encoded** keys (e.g. `fields_sub_project_sub_key`, `tenantEntityName`) |
376	>
377	> Concrete (Jira Create Issue): `bodyParameters.fields.project.key = "ENGCE"` AND `parameterValues = [["fields_sub_project_sub_key", "ENGCE"]]`. Concrete (Dataservice V3): `queryParameters.tenantEntityName = ""my-entity""` AND `parameterValues = [["tenantEntityName", ""my-entity""]]`. Dropping the runtime-input copy on the assumption that the cache covers it leaves the runtime with no field value to bind — manifests as `DAP-DT-_2003 refField with name <X> not found` at activity load.

Omitting the runtime bucket is the most common mistake — the cache alone does not feed the connector at runtime.

504	## Bindings — top-level `.flow` `bindings[]`
505	
506	When a flow uses connector nodes, the runtime needs to know **which authenticated connection** to use for each connector. Bindings are authored in the flow's **top-level `bindings[]` array** (a sibling of `nodes`, `edges`, `definitions`). At `flow debug` / `flow pack` time the CLI regenerates `content/bindings_v2.json` from these entries.
507	
508	> **Never edit `bindings_v2.json` directly.** Any manual edits are overwritten on the next debug/pack. All authoring flows through the `.flow` file's top-level `bindings[]`.
509	
510	### How connector nodes reference bindings
511	
512	The connector node's **definition** (the manifest copied from `uip maestro flow registry get` into `definitions[]`) carries a `model.context[]` template like this. **Leave the definition exactly as the registry returns it** — do NOT rewrite `<bindings.*>` placeholders inside the definition, and do NOT author `model.context[]` on the instance:
513	
514	```json
515	"context": [
516	  { "name": "connectorKey", "type": "string", "value": "uipath-atlassian-jira" },
517	  { "name": "connection", "type": "string", "value": "<bindings.uipath-atlassian-jira connection>" },
518	  { "name": "folderKey", "type": "string", "value": "<bindings.FolderKey>" }
519	]
520	```
521	
522	At BPMN emit time, the runtime rewrites each `<bindings.{name}>` placeholder to `=bindings.{id}` by finding a top-level `bindings[]` entry whose `name` matches the placeholder. For connectors the definition's `model.bindings.resourceKey` is typically unset, so matching is **name-only** within the `resource: "Connection"` candidate set.
523	
524	> **Matching differs from resource nodes.** For `uipath.core.*` resource nodes (rpa, agent, flow, agentic-process, api-workflow, hitl), the definition's `model.bindings.resourceKey` is set to `<FolderPath>.<ResourceName>`, so placeholder matching is scoped by `(name, resourceKey)`. For connector nodes, `resourceKey` on the definition is typically unset, so matching is name-only — the `<CONNECTOR_KEY> connection` placeholder must be unique per connector in the flow. Don't confuse the two patterns.
525	
526	### Top-level `bindings[]` shape (CLI-emitted; reference only)
527	
528	`uip maestro flow node configure` populates these entries — you do not author them by hand. The schema below is the shape the CLI emits, for **inspection** when debugging a flow's binding state and as the planned shape for the **No-Live-Tenant** flow's sidecar `<nodeId>.detail.json` (see § No-Live-Tenant / Planned Configuration above). Per the [Author capability — Node ownership](../../../CAPABILITY.md#node-ownership--who-authors-the-node) rules, `bindings[]` is part of the CLI-owned envelope for connector / connector-trigger / managed HTTP nodes.
529	
530	For every unique connection used in the flow, `node configure` appends **two entries** to top-level `bindings[]`:
531	
532	```json
533	"bindings": [
534	  {
535	    "id": "<CONN_BINDING_ID>",
536	    "name": "<CONNECTOR_KEY> connection",
537	    "type": "string",
538	    "resource": "Connection",
539	    "resourceKey": "<CONNECTION_UUID>",
540	    "default": "<CONNECTION_UUID>",
541	    "propertyAttribute": "ConnectionId"
542	  },
543	  {
544	    "id": "<FOLDER_BINDING_ID>",
545	    "name": "FolderKey",
546	    "type": "string",
547	    "resource": "Connection",
548	    "resourceKey": "<CONNECTION_UUID>",
549	    "default": "<FOLDER_KEY>",
550	    "propertyAttribute": "FolderKey"
551	  }
552	]
553	```
554	
555	| Field | Value |
556	|-------|-------|
557	| `id` | Unique string within the file. Descriptive (e.g. `bJiraConn`) or short random (e.g. `bKEFLMRB2`). |
558	| `name` (connection binding) | The IS connection name (e.g. `"chandu.lella@uipath.com #3"`). `uip maestro flow node configure` fetches this from IS automatically — this is the supported path. The placeholder form `"<CONNECTOR_KEY> connection"` appears in the table for reference only (e.g. when inspecting a flow whose bindings have not yet been configured); it must match the definition's `model.context[].connection` placeholder (without the `<bindings.` prefix and `>` suffix). |
559	| `name` (folder binding) | Literal `"FolderKey"` — matches `<bindings.FolderKey>`. |
560	| `type` | Always `"string"`. |
561	| `resource` | Always `"Connection"` — capital C, case-sensitive. |
562	| `resourceKey` | The connection UUID from `uip is connections list`. **Same UUID on both bindings.** |
563	| `default` | Connection binding → connection UUID. Folder binding → folder key. |
564	| `propertyAttribute` | `"ConnectionId"` or `"FolderKey"` — case matters. |
565	
566	The connector node instance carries no `model` block and no binding/context data. `uip maestro flow node configure` populates only `inputs.detail` on the instance and appends the two top-level `bindings[]` entries. The connection UUID is held on the binding entry (`resourceKey`), not on the node.
567	
568	> **CLI side-effect — duplicate empty bindings.** `node configure` currently appends placeholder entries with `resourceKey: ""` and no `default` alongside the resolved pair (4 entries per configure call instead of 2). Validate passes; they're harmless but verbose. Remove the empty pair via `Edit` after configure if you care about clean diffs.
569	
570	**Share bindings across nodes using the same connection.** If two connector nodes share the same `<CONNECTION_UUID>`, reuse the same two binding entries — do not add duplicates. Matching is by `name` only (the `<CONNECTOR_KEY> connection` placeholder is unique per connector), so any node whose definition resolves against `<bindings.<CONNECTOR_KEY> connection>` picks up the shared binding pair.
571	
572	### Single-connector example (Jira)
573

575	"bindings": [
576	  {
577	    "id": "bJiraConn",
578	    "name": "uipath-atlassian-jira connection",
579	    "type": "string",
580	    "resource": "Connection",
581	    "resourceKey": "7622a703-5d85-4b55-849b-6c02315b9e6e",
582	    "default": "7622a703-5d85-4b55-849b-6c02315b9e6e",
583	    "propertyAttribute": "ConnectionId"
584	  },
585	  {
586	    "id": "bJiraFolder",
587	    "name": "FolderKey",
588	    "type": "string",
589	    "resource": "Connection",
590	    "resourceKey": "7622a703-5d85-4b55-849b-6c02315b9e6e",
591	    "default": "a1b2c3d4-e5f6-7890-abcd-ef1234567890",

593	  }

598	
599	Two unique connections → four entries in `bindings[]` (two per connection):
600

602	"bindings": [
603	  { "id": "bJiraConn",   "name": "uipath-atlassian-jira connection",   "type": "string", "resource": "Connection", "resourceKey": "7622a703-5d85-4b55-849b-6c02315b9e6e", "default": "7622a703-5d85-4b55-849b-6c02315b9e6e", "propertyAttribute": "ConnectionId" },
604	  { "id": "bJiraFolder", "name": "FolderKey",                          "type": "string", "resource": "Connection", "resourceKey": "7622a703-5d85-4b55-849b-6c02315b9e6e", "default": "folder-uuid-for-jira",                "propertyAttribute": "FolderKey" },

606	  { "id": "bSlackFolder","name": "FolderKey",                          "type": "string", "resource": "Connection", "resourceKey": "a1b2c3d4-e5f6-7890-abcd-ef1234567890", "default": "folder-uuid-for-slack",               "propertyAttribute": "FolderKey" }
607	]

610	Both `FolderKey` entries share the same `name` but have distinct `resourceKey`s — that's how the runtime keeps them separate.
611	
612	### Generated `bindings_v2.json` (reference only — do not edit)
613	
614	At debug/pack time, the CLI derives `content/bindings_v2.json` from the top-level `bindings[]` above. One `Connection` resource per unique `resourceKey`; the `FolderKey` bindings are absorbed as metadata (they do not produce standalone resource entries). The generated output looks like:
615	
616	```json
617	{
618	  "version": "2.0",
619	  "resources": [
620	    {
621	      "resource": "Connection",
622	      "key": "7622a703-5d85-4b55-849b-6c02315b9e6e",
623	      "id": "Connection7622a703-5d85-4b55-849b-6c02315b9e6e",
624	      "value": {
625	        "ConnectionId": {
626	          "defaultValue": "7622a703-5d85-4b55-849b-6c02315b9e6e",
627	          "isExpression": false,
628	          "displayName": "my-jira-connection"
629	        }
630	      },
631	      "metadata": {
632	        "ActivityName": "Create Issue",
633	        "BindingsVersion": "2.2",
634	        "DisplayLabel": "my-jira-connection",
635	        "UseConnectionService": "true",

637	      }
638	    }
639	  ]
640	}
641	```
642	
643	- `id` is always `"Connection" + <resourceKey>` (concatenated, no separator) — generated, not authored.
644	- `metadata.Connector` is derived from the definition's `model.context[].connectorKey`.
645	- `metadata.ActivityName` comes from the matched node's `display.label`.
646	
647	### Other binding resource types (triggers, queues, scheduled)
648	
649	For connector-trigger flows, the same pattern applies — top-level `bindings[]` entries with additional metadata; the CLI derives `EventTrigger` and `Property` resources for `bindings_v2.json`. See [connector-trigger/impl.md](../connector-trigger/impl.md) for the trigger-specific shape.

651	| Generated `bindings_v2.json` resource | Authored via | Key source fields |
652	|---------------------------------------|--------------|-------------------|
653	| `Connection` | Top-level `bindings[]` with `resource: "Connection"`, `propertyAttribute: "ConnectionId"` | Covered above |
654	| `EventTrigger` | Top-level `bindings[]` + the trigger node itself | See connector-trigger plugin |
655	| `Property` | Trigger node's `model.inputs.filterFields` | See connector-trigger plugin |
656	| `Queue` / `TimeTrigger` | Specific trigger types | See relevant trigger plugin |

658	> **Never hardcode connection IDs.** Always fetch them from IS at authoring time. Connection IDs are tenant-specific and change across environments.

Re-run `uip maestro flow node configure` on the affected connector node(s) so the CLI re-emits top-level `bindings[]`; `bindings_v2.json` is regenerated from those at the next debug/pack. Compare the emitted shape against the CLI-emitted reference in § Top-level `bindings[]` shape. |

The runtime side works but Studio Web has no tree to render. | Re-run `uip maestro flow node configure` with `--detail '{"filter": {...tree...}}'` — the CLI populates both halves. See Step 6a above and [uipath-platform — Filter Trees (CEQL)](../../../../../../uipath-platform/references/integration-service/activities.md#filter-trees-ceql). |
679	| `node configure` fails with `'<name>' is a FilterBuilder parameter — pass a structured filter tree under --detail.filter` | Same root cause — raw string under `queryParameters` for a FilterBuilder param | Move the value into `--detail.filter` as a structured tree. The CLI catches this at configure time so it never reaches Studio Web. |
680	| `node configure` fails with `customFieldsRequestDetails.parameterValues must be an array of [key, value] tuples, not an object map` | Wrote `parameterValues: {key: value}` (object map). Studio Web emits its `Map<string,string\|null>` as `Array.from(entries())` — tuples, not object | Convert to tuples: `[["key", "value"], ...]`. See Step 6c. |
681	| Custom fields fault at runtime with token unresolved | A `{token}` in `objectActions[].apiConfiguration.url` or `body` has no entry in `parameterValues` | Re-read the ObjectAction's `apiConfiguration` placeholders, add the missing tuple to `parameterValues`. CLI does not validate token coverage. |
682	| `node configure` fails with `customFieldsRequestDetails has unknown keys: ObjectActionName, ParameterValues` | PascalCase inner keys instead of camelCase | Use `objectActionName` / `parameterValues`. Studio Web emits camelCase; PascalCase is rejected. |
683	| Field rejected at runtime as unknown (e.g. `"unknown field 'fields.labels[*]'"`) after a clean `flow validate` | `[*]` was left in the `bodyParameters` / `queryParameters` / `pathParameters` key. `[*]` is an array marker from `requestFields[].name`, not part of the wire key. | Strip `[*]` from the key in your `--detail` payload, pass an array value matching the field's `dataType`, and re-run `node configure`. 685	### Debug Tips

1	# Connections
2	
3	Connections are authenticated sessions for a specific connector. They store credentials and tokens, and can be shared across automations within a folder.
4	
5	> Full command syntax and options: [uip-commands.md — Integration Service](../uip-commands.md#integration-service-is). Domain-specific usage patterns are shown inline below.
6	
7	---
8	
9	## Response Fields
10	
11	| Field | Show to user? | Description |
12	|---|---|---|
13	| **`Name`** | **Yes** | Display name — always use this as the primary identifier when presenting to the user (e.g., "Salesforce Prod", "bai.li") |
14	| **`State`** | **Yes** | `Enabled` or other status. Only Enabled connections can be used. |
15	| **`IsDefault`** | **Yes** | `Yes` or `No`. Recommend the default connection but always let the user confirm. |
16	| **`Owner`** | **Yes** | Who created the connection (email) |
17	| **`Folder`** | **Yes** | Folder name this connection belongs to (e.g., "Shared", "Personal") |
18	| `ConnectorName` | **Yes** | Human-readable connector name (e.g., "Slack", "Salesforce") |
19	| `ByoaConnection` | **Yes** | `Yes` or `No`. BYOA (Bring Your Own Account) connection — customer registered their own OAuth app with the external service. Required for some webhook triggers. |
20	| `Id` | Internal | Connection UUID — use only in `--connection-id` CLI args, never show to user |
21	| `ConnectorKey` | Internal | Connector key — use only in CLI args |
22	| `FolderKey` | Internal | Folder UUID — use only in `--folder-key` CLI args, never show to user |
23	| `ElementInstanceId` | Internal | Numeric instance ID — use only in `--element-instance-id` for `uip is webhooks config` |
24	
25	---
26	
27	## Command Syntax
28	
29	`<connector-key>` is a **positional argument**, not a flag:
30	
31	```bash
32	# Correct — always pass --all-folders for discovery (see Folder Scoping below)
33	uip is connections list "uipath-salesforce-slack" --all-folders --output json
34	
35	# WRONG — there is no --connector-key flag
36	uip is connections list --connector-key "uipath-salesforce-slack"
37	```
38	
39	**Always pass a connector key.** Running `uip is connections list` with no arg returns a noisy, paginated list across every connector in the tenant and is not a useful survey step.
40	
41	**Wrong key?** If the call errors with "connector not found" or returns empty unexpectedly, look up the correct key:
42	
43	```bash
44	uip is connectors list --filter "<vendor>" --output json
45	```
46	
47	Connector keys are prefixed by source — `uipath-<vendor>-<service>` for catalog connectors, `custom-entity-*` for tenant-built. See [connectors.md — Connector Disambiguation](connectors.md#connector-disambiguation) for the full classification ladder.
48	
49	---
50	
51	## Selecting a Connection
52	
53	### Connector-Specific Overrides
54	
55	**Before applying the auto-select rule below, check this table.** If the connector key (and node-type pattern, where listed) matches an entry, read the linked file and follow its rules. Override supersedes the auto-select rule.
56	
57	| Connector key | Applies when | Override action | Detail |
58	|---|---|---|---|
59	| `uipath-microsoft-teams` | `send-bot-*` activity node types | Ask user; warn that bot scope is required | [uipath-microsoft-teams.md → Connection Selection Override](connector-overrides/uipath-microsoft-teams.md#connection-selection-override) |
60	| `uipath-salesforce-slack` | Webhook trigger node types (allow-list — excludes `button-clicked`) | Ask user; filter `--byoa` from the start | [uipath-salesforce-slack.md → Connection Selection Override](connector-overrides/uipath-salesforce-slack.md#connection-selection-override) |
61	
62	To add a new override, see [connector-overrides/README.md](connector-overrides/README.md).
63	
64	---
65	
66	**Auto-select rule (no prompt) — when all three hold:**
67	
68	- `IsDefault: Yes`
69	- `State: Enabled`
70	- `Folder` is the user's personal workspace
71	
72	Bind silently and skip the presentation steps below.
73	
74	Detect the user's personal workspace once per session — list all folders and filter for the personal type:
75	
76	```bash
77	uip or folders list --all --output json
78	# → Data: [{ Name, Key, Path, Description, Type, ParentKey }]
79	# Filter entries where Type == "Personal"
80	```
81	
82	Match `connection.FolderKey` against the personal workspace's `Key`. If the call returns multiple personal workspaces (admin tenant) or no match, fall through to the presentation flow.
83	
84	**Otherwise — present connections to the user.** Recommend the default but let the user confirm.
85	
86	### Folder Scoping (`--all-folders`)
87	
88	**Always pass `--all-folders` when discovering connections.** Without it, the CLI returns the active folder only — producing false "no connections found" results when the connection exists in another folder you can see. After the user picks a connection, capture its `FolderKey` from the response for downstream binding; do not pass `--folder-key` during discovery.
89	
90	- `--all-folders`: spans every folder you have access to. Works with or without a `<connector-key>` positional.
91	- **Mutually exclusive with `--folder` / `--folder-key`** — passing both fails with `Result: Failure`, `Message: "Conflicting folder flags..."`, exit code 1.
92	
93	### For Native Connectors
94	
95	1. List connections for the connector across all folders:
96	
97	   ```bash
98	   uip is connections list "<connector-key>" --all-folders --output json
99	   ```
100	
101	2. Present all enabled connections to the user using **Name, Owner, and Folder** (never UUIDs), **recommending** the default (`IsDefault: Yes`, `State: Enabled`):
102	   - "I found these connections: 1) **Salesforce Prod** by user@example.com (default, enabled, Shared folder) ← recommended 2) **Salesforce Dev** by admin@example.com (enabled, Shared folder). Which should I use?"
103	3. If only one enabled connection exists, still confirm: "I found connection **<Name>** by <Owner> in **<Folder>** folder (default, enabled). Should I use this one?"
104	4. **Verify health — ping after every selection** (auto-select and user-confirmed alike):
105	
106	   ```bash
107	   uip is connections ping "<connection-id>" --output json
108	   ```
109	
110	   If ping fails or reports not Enabled, follow step 5.
111	
112	5. If not enabled (from list `State` or ping result) → prompt user to re-authenticate via `is connections edit <id>`, then re-ping.
113	
114	6. **No connections in step 1 — bypass the cache before concluding none exist:**
115	   1. Retry with `--refresh`:
116	      ```bash
117	      uip is connections list "<connector-key>" --all-folders --refresh --output json
118	      ```
119	   2. If still empty, prompt user to create one via `uip is connections create "<connector-key>"`.
120	
121	### For BYOA Connections (Webhook Triggers)
122	
123	BYOA (Bring Your Own Account) connections use an OAuth app the customer registered with the external service (e.g., a Slack app they own). Some webhook triggers require BYOA; many do not. **The requirement is per event object, not per connector** — read it from the `triggers objects` response.
124	
125	**Decision flow:**
126	
127	1. Get any enabled connection — needed only as `--connection-id` for the next call:
128	
129	   ```bash
130	   uip is connections list "<connector-key>" --all-folders --output json
131	   ```
132	
133	2. Query trigger objects and read the `byoaConnection` flag for the matching event:
134	
135	   ```bash
136	   uip is triggers objects "<connector-key>" "<OPERATION>" \
137	     --connection-id "<id>" --output json
138	   ```
139	
140	3. **If `byoaConnection: true`** — the connection from step 1 is not usable. Filter to BYOA across all folders:
141	
142	   ```bash
143	   uip is connections list "<connector-key>" --byoa --all-folders --output json
144	   ```
145	
146	   If empty, retry with `--refresh` to bypass the CLI cache:
147	
148	   ```bash
149	   uip is connections list "<connector-key>" --byoa --all-folders --refresh --output json
150	   ```
151	
152	   If still empty, **stop and tell the user**: "This trigger requires a BYOA connection for `<connector-key>`. None found. Create one in the Integration Service portal or with `uip is connections create "<connector-key>"`, then re-run."
153	
154	4. **If `byoaConnection: false`** — use the connection from step 1. Verify health with `uip is connections ping "<id>" --output json`.
155	
156	> Connector-specific OAuth-app setup instructions (e.g., what permissions a Slack app needs) come from the trigger's `design.textBlocks` field in the `triggers objects` response. Surface that text to the user verbatim — do not invent service-specific guidance.
157	
158	For webhook URL retrieval after the trigger is configured, see [triggers.md — Webhook URL Retrieval](triggers.md#webhook-url-retrieval).
159	
160	### For HTTP Fallback
161	
162	1. List connections for `uipath-uipath-http`
163	2. Look for a connection whose **Name** contains the target vendor (case-insensitive substring match, e.g., "Apify" matches "Apify", "Apify - Prod", "My Apify Connection")
164	3. Present matches to the user. If multiple matches → let them choose.
165	4. If no match → present all existing HTTP connections and ask the user to choose, or offer to create a new one
166	
167	> **Note:** Name-based matching is best-effort. If connection names don't follow vendor naming conventions, present all HTTP connections to the user.
168	
169	---
170	
171	## Folder Scoping
172	
173	`uip is connections list <connector-key>` defaults to filtering by the **current** folder context — results from other folders (including the user's personal workspace) are silently excluded. Empty response on the filtered side looks like:
174	
175	```json
176	{"Message":"No connections found for connector '<connector-key>'."}
177	```
178	
179	even though a connection exists in another folder.
180	
181	**Cross-folder pattern** — pass `--folder` explicitly:
182	
183	```bash
184	uip is connections list "<connector-key>" --folder "<folder-name-or-key>" --output json
185	```
186	
187	**Enumerate every folder** — iterate folders and list per folder:
188	
189	```bash
190	uip or folders list --output json
191	# → for each folder, call:
192	uip is connections list "<connector-key>" --folder "<folder-name-or-key>" --output json
193	```
194	
195	> If the user reports "connection exists in my personal workspace but CLI can't see it", suspect default folder filtering — re-list with `--folder` set to that workspace before creating a new connection.
196	
197	---
198	
199	## Identifying a JDBC Connection's Target DB
200	
201	For the JDBC gateway connector (`uipath-uipath-jdbc`, "Database Hub"), `connections list` does **not** expose `jdbcUrl` or `driverClass` — config is intentionally hidden. The only signal for "what DB does this JDBC connection point to?" is the connection **`name`**.
202	
203	Match case-insensitively (weak signal — surface as "likely <DB>", never "is <DB>"):
204	
205	| DB | Substrings in `connection.name` |
206	|---|---|
207	| Snowflake | `snowflake`, `sf` |
208	| Databricks | `databricks`, `dbx` |
209	| Postgres | `postgres`, `postgresql`, `pg` |
210	| MySQL | `mysql` |
211	| SQL Server | `sqlserver`, `mssql` |
212	| Oracle | `oracle` |
213	| Redshift | `redshift` |
214	| BigQuery | `bigquery`, `bq` |
215	
216	If the user explicitly named a connection in their prompt (e.g. "use the `pat_databricks` connection"), that overrides name-matching — bind it directly.
217	
218	Used by the [connectors.md — JDBC Gateway](connectors.md#jdbc-gateway--database-sql-intent) decision matrix.
219	
220	---
221	
222	## Getting a Connection's Vendor Base URL
223	
224	`uip is connections base-url <connection-id>` returns the exact vendor base URL the connection uses for proxied calls (e.g., raw `http-request` calls, Managed HTTP Request in connector mode). Manual-mode invocations don't use it. The connection must be Enabled.
225	
226	```bash
227	uip is connections base-url "<connection-id>" --output json
228	# → { "Result": "Success", "Code": "ConnectionBaseUrl",
229	#     "Data": { "ConnectionId": "<id>", "BaseUrl": "https://..." } }
230	```
231	
232	Examples across connectors:
233	
234	| Connector | Returned `BaseUrl` |
235	|---|---|
236	| `uipath-atlassian-jira` | `https://api.atlassian.com/ex/jira/<site-id>/rest/api/2` |
237	| `uipath-microsoft-outlook365` | `https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0` |
238	| `uipath-uipath-marketo` | `https://<account>.mktorest.com/rest` |
239	
240	Use this whenever you need to compose a relative `url` for `http-request` or Managed HTTP Request in connector mode. See [http-request.md](http-request.md).
241	
242	---
243	
244	## Scope-Related Errors
245	
246	A connection can be `Enabled` but lack optional OAuth scopes needed for specific activities. This typically surfaces as a **403 Forbidden** error during execute.
247	
248	**Symptoms:**
249	- Connection pings successfully (`State: Enabled`)
250	- Execute fails with 403 or a vendor-specific "insufficient permissions" error
251	- The same operation works with a different connection that has broader scopes
252	
253	**Recovery:**
254	1. Inform the user that the connection may need broader OAuth scopes for this activity
255	2. Re-authorize with broader scopes: `uip is connections edit <connection-id>`
256	3. After re-auth, ping again to verify, then retry the operation

1	# Managed HTTP Request - Concept + `http-request` Authoring Helper
2	
3	This doc covers two things every agent authoring a Managed HTTP Request needs to know:
4	1. What Managed HTTP Request is, and the two modes it runs in.
5	2. How to use the `http-request` CLI command to fill in the values Managed HTTP Request needs.
6	
7	Consumers: Maestro Flow, Maestro BPMN, API Workflows, Case Management, etc. Each consumer surfaces Managed HTTP Request differently (as a node, an activity, a tool call, …) and uses its own type identifier and configuration schema - the concept and the rules below are the same. For the exact node/activity type identifier and how to configure it, see your consumer's own authoring docs.
8	
9	## What is Managed HTTP Request?
10	
11	A built-in way to make an HTTP call from a UiPath automation. Runs in two modes - **connector mode** and **manual mode**:
12	
13	| Mode | When | `url` | Auth |
14	|---|---|---|---|
15	| **Connector** | Connector exists for the vendor but the specific operation is not curated | **Relative** to the connection's vendor base URL | Applied automatically from the bound connection |
16	| **Manual** | No connector exists, or public API with no auth needed | **Full URL** | You supply all headers, including auth |
17	
18	## Connector-Mode Rules
19	
20	- **Connector mode only works if the connector supports HTTP request activity** — verify by running `uip is connectors get "<connector-key>"` and checking the `HasHttpRequest` flag.
21	- `url` must be **relative**. Wrong: `"url": "https://example.atlassian.net/rest/api/2/issue"`. Right: `"url": "/issue"`.
22	- The connection's base URL is prepended automatically.
23	- The auth header is applied automatically - do not set `Authorization`.
24	- **`application/json` only - request and response.** No other content type is supported. File upload/download operations are the most common violation (`multipart/form-data`, `application/octet-stream`, binary/stream responses) - check the operation's request and response content types before authoring. If non-JSON, connector mode cannot call it - use a curated connector activity; if none exists, surface to the user.
25	- Get the exact vendor base URL for a connection via (so you can compose the relative `url` correctly):
26	
27	```bash
28	uip is connections base-url "<connection-id>" --output json
29	# → { "Data": { "BaseUrl": "https://api.atlassian.com/ex/jira/<site>/rest/api/2" } }
30	```
31	
32	## Manual-Mode Rules
33	
34	- `url` is the **fully qualified URL**.
35	- No connection is bound - you supply everything needed to make the call: URL, headers (including auth if needed), query params, and body.
36	
37	## Step 0: Ground Against the Vendor's API Docs (registry) — connector mode only
38	
39	> **Connector mode only.** This grounding step applies when `authentication: "connector"` (a connector exists and the `url` is **relative** to its vendor base URL). Manual mode targets an arbitrary REST API with a full URL and has no connector to look up — skip this step for manual mode.
40	
41	**Before composing any `url` / `query` / `body`, ground the endpoint against the vendor's documentation.** Skipping this is the most common cause of a wrong-but-plausible endpoint that still "completes" at runtime (many vendors return HTTP 200 with an error body for an unknown path — e.g. Slack `{"ok":false,"error":"unknown_method"}` — so a bad path does not fault).
42	
43	1. Look the target connector up in [`vendor-docs-registry.json`](vendor-docs-registry.json) (same directory). Match by `connectorKey`.
44	2. **If listed:** read its `docsUrl` (authoritative API reference) and `notes` (vendor-specific conventions: endpoint shape, custom-field keys, query quirks). Honor the `notes` verbatim, then confirm the exact path with the `http-request` probe below (the live call is the final authority — the registry only grounds the baseline).
45	3. **If NOT listed:** this registry-grounding step does not apply. Proceed with the normal authoring flow — resolve the endpoint and any missing values via the `http-request` probe below, as you would otherwise.
46	
47	> **Pass endpoint paths verbatim — do NOT "REST-ify" them.** Many vendor APIs name operations with **literal dots**, where the whole dotted token is a single path segment: Slack`chat.postMessage`, `conversations.replies`. The dot is **not** a namespace separator — never rewrite `chat.postMessage` as `/chat/postMessage`. Copy the method exactly as the docs/registry show it (`"url": "/chat.postMessage"`).
48	
49	## Authoring Helper: `http-request` command
50	
51	Authoring a Managed HTTP Request payload requires concrete vendor values - IDs, field names, endpoint paths. Use `http-request` command to call any vendor API directly through the connection - same auth, same base URL the Managed HTTP Request will use at runtime.
52	
53	### When the Agent Needs `http-request` command
54	
55	Use `http-request` command to resolve any of the following before authoring the Managed HTTP Request payload:
56	
57	- **Identifier lookups.** Resolve a human-friendly name to the vendor's internal ID. Examples: project key from a project name, channel ID from a channel name, user ID from email/name, custom-field IDs.
58	- **Required and optional fields** the vendor expects in the request body
59	- **Endpoint paths, query params, pagination tokens** before committing to a payload
60	- **Vendor error responses** for unsupported parameters or permissions
61	
62	### Command
63	
64	```bash
65	uip is resources run create "<connector-key>" http-request \
66	  --connection-id "<id>" \
67	  --body '{"method":"<method>","url":"<relative-path>"}' --output json
68	```
69	
70	| `body` field | Required | Notes |
71	|---|---|---|
72	| `method` | Yes | Uppercase HTTP verb |
73	| `url` | Yes | **Relative** to the connection's vendor base URL (same convention as Managed HTTP Request connector mode) |
74	| `headers` | No | Extra headers. Do NOT set `Authorization`. |
75	| `body` | For POST/PUT/PATCH | **Stringified** JSON. Only `application/json` is supported today — no other content type. |
76	
77	`http-request` command uses the same connection that Managed HTTP Request will use at runtime, so auth + base URL are applied automatically - same convention as Managed HTTP Request itself.
78	
79	### Read-Only During Authoring
80	
81	When using the `http-request` command, use `GET` method only, as `POST` / `PATCH` / `PUT` / `DELETE` mutate vendor state, often irreversibly.
82	
83	Exception: the user asks you to actually run the operation now, not just author it.
84	
85	## Worked Example: Jira Create Issue
86	
87	User wants to create a Jira issue. Before composing the Managed HTTP Request payload, the agent needs the project key, issue type ID, and required custom fields. All resolved via `http-request` command GETs.
88	
89	```bash
90	# 1. Resolve project key (user said "Engineering project").
91	uip is resources run create uipath-atlassian-jira http-request \
92	  --connection-id "<id>" \
93	  --body '{"method":"GET","url":"/project/search?query=Engineering"}' --output json
94	# → key "ENG"
95	
96	# 2. For project ENG, get available issue types + required custom fields.
97	uip is resources run create uipath-atlassian-jira http-request \
98	  --connection-id "<id>" \
99	  --body '{"method":"GET","url":"/issue/createmeta?projectKeys=ENG&expand=projects.issuetypes.fields"}' \
100	  --output json
101	# → match "Task" → id "10001"; required custom field: customfield_10010 (Story Points)
102	```
103	
104	3. (Optional) Confirm resolved values with the user.
105	
106	4. Compose the Managed HTTP Request payload. The actual configuration command and schema are consumer-specific — the request body Managed HTTP Request will send to Jira at runtime looks like:
107	
108	```json
109	{
110	  "method": "POST",
111	  "url": "/issue",
112	  "body": {
113	    "fields": {
114	      "project": { "key": "ENG" },
115	      "issuetype": { "id": "10001" },
116	      "summary": "Fix coder evals",
117	      "customfield_10010": 3
118	    }
119	  }
120	}
121	```
122	
123	All steps 1-2 are GETs because we are in the authoring phase. The POST to `/issue` happens at runtime, performed by Managed HTTP Request - never by CLI during authoring.
124	
125	## Critical Rules
126	
127	1. **Do NOT set the `Authorization` header manually in connector mode.** Auth is applied automatically by the connection. Setting it yourself can leak or override the token.
128	2. **Do NOT use an absolute URL in connector-mode `url`.** Wrong: `"url": "https://example.atlassian.net/rest/api/2/project"`. Right: `"url": "/project"`.
129	3. **Do NOT issue writes via CLI during authoring.** See "Read-Only During Authoring" above.
130	4. **Do NOT guess the base URL.** Use `uip is connections base-url <connection-id>`.
131	5. **(Connector mode) Ground the endpoint before authoring.** Look the vendor up in [`vendor-docs-registry.json`](vendor-docs-registry.json), read its `docsUrl` + `notes`, and confirm the path with the `http-request` probe. See [Step 0](#step-0-ground-against-the-vendors-api-docs-registry--connector-mode-only).
132	6. **(Connector mode) Pass endpoint paths verbatim.** 
133	7. **In connector mode, request and response bodies are `application/json` only.** No other content type is supported; do NOT set `Content-Type` to anything else. Same rule applies to the `http-request` helper command body (it runs through a connection). Manual mode has no such limit — you supply your own `Content-Type` and body.
